subject: res-ipc-endpoints
text: - **Linux / macOS:** Unix domain socket file `<socket dir>/viola-<h12>.sock` in a per-user 0700 directory (security-plan arch amendment 2): `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola/` on Linux, `$TMPDIR/viola/` on macOS, and `/tmp/viola-<uid>/` only as a fallback; never the `/tmp` or `$TMPDIR` root. The socket is chmod 0600 after the bind. The start arbiter is the sibling `<socket dir>/viola-<h12>.lock`: `run` holds an exclusive lock on it, and a held lock is the taken-name refusal. `run` resolves the path once and records it as `endpoint` in the instance snapshot. Every other process (`hook`, `mcp`, CLI verbs, and `run`'s collision check) connects to the recorded `endpoint`, because processes spawned inside the session may run with a different environment from the wrapper. It rebuilds the path by the same rule only when the snapshot is missing or unreadable. Linux abstract-namespace names are never used, because they carry no filesystem permissions and any local user could connect (see Local endpoint trust boundary).

subject: res-ipc-endpoints
text: - Before its first frame each process that connects to the recorded `endpoint`, but `run`'s collision check (`hook`'s event and dialog paths, the CLI frame verbs `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release` / `link` / `unlink`, and `mcp`'s four frame tools), checks that the process serving it is the snapshot's wrapper: the connected stream's peer pid (`viola_channel::Client::server_pid` / `TokioClient::server_pid`) and its OS start time against the snapshot's `pid` and `started_at` (§Standard Contracts, Session liveness). A mismatch or a check that cannot be made sends no frame: CLI exit 21 `instance-unreachable`, MCP `instance-unreachable`, the hook failing open. macOS reports no peer pid and stays on the recorded gap.

subject: res-env-vars
text: - `VIOLA_DIR`: the absolute path of the instance's state directory (`<viola home>/instances/<ViolaName>/`), set by `viola run` in the child. It is read by `hook` (for the recorded `endpoint`, the SessionEnd direct-append fallback, the statusline wrapper and the diagnostics directory) and by `mcp` and every CLI verb run inside the session. Each derives the viola home as the grandparent of `VIOLA_DIR`, so a session started with `--home` keeps its hooks, MCP server and nested CLI calls in that home. As landed (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract), `hook` and every CLI verb, `run` and `revive` included, read it: the verbs through `resolved_home`, which takes the `VIOLA_DIR` grandparent only when `VIOLA_NAME` and `VIOLA_DIR` pass `instance_of`'s shape check, a pair that fails falling through to the default, never refusing (§Cross-cutting Patterns, Config management); `viola mcp` (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers) resolves its home through the same `resolved_home` and reads `VIOLA_NAME` for its own name (the `from` it adds and its detail sink).

subject: res-filesystem
res-filesystem
text:
- `instances/<ViolaName>/events.ndjson`, `events.ndjson.lock`, `snapshot.json`, `snapshot.json.lock`, `heartbeat`, `settings.json` (the per-session settings override that wraps the statusline; Unix only, see Claude Code integration names), `diagnostics/` (the owner-only content-bearing detail files `detail-<role>.ndjson`, such as the panic payload and backtrace in `detail-run.ndjson`; dir 0700, files 0600 on Unix; one `write` per line; file format owned by obs and fixed by `schemas/diag-detail.v1.json`. Codes-only process lines go to the home-level role files). v1 never rotates or truncates `events.ndjson`, because `wait`'s `after` and `send`'s `cursor` are byte offsets into it. Bounding its size is an open item, and any scheme must keep existing offsets valid. Four readers check these files before they use them (`viola list`, `viola revive`, `hook statusline`, and `viola link` / `viola unlink` sharing one check). `viola list` (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list): `viola_state::board::scan` runs `check_path` on the home and on `instances/`, each that exists (absent passes, an unstattable one is refused), reads each entry's type without following a link (a link, a non-directory or a name that is no `ViolaName` gives no instance and is only counted), joins a path only from a parsed name, then runs `check_instance` per instance in name order, all before any file under the home is opened and before its log starts; the first failure refuses the whole board with exit 21 (`--json`: `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` on stdout, stderr empty; human: the instance-state or the home-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair on stderr, stdout empty), no log opened, no line written and the home's mode left as found — the founder's own answer, 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer (the operator's answer at that chunk's planning, superseded 2026-10-13).
 `viola revive` (the start arm and `--list`) runs `viola_state::strict::check_instance` over the home, `instances/`, the instance directory, its `snapshot.json` and its `events.ndjson`, each that exists and in that order, before its wrapper log opens, and a refusal is exit 1 with the state-files `unable:` / `hint:` pair (under `--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"strict-modes-failed","detail":null}` document on stdout, stderr empty): no log opened, no line written (no `process-start`, no `process-exit`), no child started and the home's mode left as found. `viola hook statusline` runs the same check on its canonicalised instance directory before anything under the home is read or opened; a refused instance returns exit 0 at once with no `config.json` read, no role file opened, no `hook-invoked` or `hook-decision` line, no stdin read, no command run, nothing printed and `budget.json` untouched. Neither arm writes the word `strict-modes-failed` on any line. `viola link` / `viola unlink` run `check_instance` on the home and `instances/<driven>` before `client::start`, so before any role file or log opens and before any snapshot value is read; a refusal is exit 21 (`--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` document on stdout, stderr empty; human the instance-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair on stderr), no line written and the mode left as found. Each of these checks comes first because opening a log sets an existing home to 0700 (as measured on the statusline arm at chunk 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through, `evidence/red-green.md` §3), and a check made after it passes a home at 0770. Both orders were fixed at chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor: before it `revive`'s start arm opened its log first, and a home at 0770 came back 0700 and passed the check (as measured at that chunk's `research.md`, runs C and D, and `evidence/red-green.md` (a)), and the statusline arm opened its log after a refused check, so its refusal lasted one invocation (`evidence/red-green.md` (b)). That a refused check leaves no trace on the statusline arm is the founder's own answer, 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer (the operator's answer at that chunk's planning, superseded 2026-10-13). `check_instance` has these three product call sites (`src/cmd/hook/statusline.rs`, `src/cmd/revive.rs` and `src/cmd/link.rs`, the one site both link verbs share; the rule: `check_instance(` under `src/`).
 The check is proven on Unix (five widened modes). No case widens the DACL of an instance tree on Windows yet; that case is owed to the working-route entry "Home and code-bearing file integrity".

subject: res-filesystem
text: - `ledger/stamps.json` + `ledger/stamps.json.lock`: `viola verify` stamps (CLI version → each ledger row's `pass`/`fail`, plus the values measured for that version: `largest_hook_payload` per spine event and `typed_probe`, the interactive runs' ready and turn settle times, prompt latency, largest turn gap and `/compact` answer latency, which validate the compiled gate and window constants (the compact latency against `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW`), and `dialog_probe.parallel_both_before_first_post`, read from Run C's captures; `run` reads none of them), in the Ledger stamps envelope (Standard Contracts). `ledger/` is 0700 and both files 0600 on Unix. The ONE writer is `viola_state::stamps::update_stamps`, called only by `viola verify`: it holds the `.lock` for the read-modify-write, reads the current bytes under the `MAX_FRAME` cap and replaces through `replace_private`. Readers use `read_stamps` (no lock; over the cap is an error), except `run`'s version gate, which reads through `read_stamps_strict` (the `viola_state::strict` check first: owner-only modes on Unix, owner + DACL on Windows); a refusal records `cli_verified:false` and one `parse-rejected{parser:"ledger-stamps", detail:"strict-modes-failed"}`. The rows themselves (probes and expected post-conditions) are compiled into `viola-agent-claude`. Read by `run`'s version gate.

subject: res-filesystem
text: - Test-only, outside the viola home: `<temp dir>/viola-root-watch/<test name, :: → .>.<label>.report` — the root test support `tests/support/watch.rs` `Watch` (bound `WITHIN` = 7 s, shared by the root waits on a child: `Instant::now() + WITHIN` reads 28 sites in 20 files under `tests/`, as measured at chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor's wrap on the Linux dev host's final tree (two more than at chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive: one each in `tests/cli_budget.rs`, a new file, and `tests/cli_revive.rs`), the shared `tests/support/events.rs` and `tests/support/cli.rs` holding one each; that pattern is the count's rule and not a census of every wait on the bound. One of the waits is `tests/support/home.rs` `wait_endpoint_gone`, which `Wrapper::stop` / `stop_keep` run after the wrapper's exit until the snapshot's recorded `endpoint` is unconnectable; after a kill, `Wrapper::kill` waits on `holder_gone` instead (on Unix a connect to the path is refused or the path is absent, on Windows the pipe is not found), because a killed wrapper removes nothing and its socket file stays on Unix, where the stop path's rule is the file being absent (as measured at chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive, the kill-and-revive case green on the three CI runners)). It is created empty at the wait's start and gets a line only when the polled state changes (codes, counts and booleans only), so a test the runner kills keeps its evidence. It is kept when the test panics or is killed and removed when it passes. `viola` never reads or writes it.

subject: res-repository
text:
- `target/e2e-home/viola-session-*/home` (harness sessions, stamped at `boot` step 4 by `viola verify` against the fake agent unless `--unstamped`), `target/e2e-home/viola-test-*/home` (root rstest homes, `tests/support/home.rs`; the `stamped_home` fixture stamps through `viola verify` against the fake agent at the recorded 2.1.287) and `target/e2e-home/viola-live-<pid>/home` (the one real-`claude` `viola verify` of the local-only `run --local-live`, never under `CI`): every harness and test home but the one `viola-chaos-*` home of `tests/chaos_feed_panic.rs` (Filesystem, above), gitignored and kept in CI for the obs gates (never under `run --mutants`, which keeps no home). Each `viola-test-*` dir holds `owner.json` `{pid, started_at}` beside `home`; a new test home first removes, when no `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_*` is set, only the dirs whose recorded owner process is gone (pid dead, or alive with another start time) — never by age or name, never a dir without a record. Both removals, the test home's own drop and that sweep, go through `remove_owned` (`tests/support/home.rs`), which deletes `owner.json` last, so a removal that stops part-way keeps the record for a later sweep. The base `target/e2e-home` is prepared before a home is made, by two test-side keepers that hold one contract: `prepare_home_base` (`tests/support/home.rs`, called from `TestHome::new`) and `Workspace::ensure_e2e_home` (the harness, called from `boot`'s start and from `run --local-live` after its build; the readers and the remover do not call it). A plain base (absent, or a directory) is created as a directory, as before. On Unix a base that is a link must have an absolute target; that target is made with mode 0700 when it is gone (one non-recursive create, never a chmod after, never a parent) and is accepted only when one `lstat` reads a real directory with no group or other bit.
 A linked base whose filesystem reads less than `HEADROOM_FLOOR_MIB` (9 GiB) free by `statvfs` (`f_bavail × f_frsize`) is refused too, with the fixed message `e2e-home backing: {free} MiB free, below the {floor} MiB floor` (the two counts, no path); the floor is one compiled constant per keeper, equal in both and set by no variable, flag or config key, its basis the tmpfs's EDQUOT reading of about 8 GiB free plus 1 GiB (as measured at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-20-epoch-5-cleanup/evidence/headroom.md`). Anything else refuses the start with a fixed message that names no path: the root keeper panics, and the harness keeper's error reads the existing `build-failed` at `boot` and `verify-exit-none` at `run --local-live` (no reason added). On Windows the keepers are the plain create. On the Linux dev host `target/e2e-home` is such a link, to the tmpfs backing `/tmp/viola-e2e-home-<uid>` (Filesystem, above): an environment fact the builder set with `mv`, `mkdir -m 700` and `ln -s`, not harness code, and no variable, flag or config key names it. It is there so a start's pinned copy does not wait on the shared volume's dirty-page budget, as measured at chunk 2026-10-07-test-homes-off-the-contended-volume `evidence/contended-reading.ndjson`: inside another project's build, five 52 MB writes at once read a 10.999 s median on the shared volume and 0.285 s at most through the link, with the verify-driven test binary green in the same window. The path string is unchanged for all three home classes.
 Through the link the owner sweep, a test home's drop and harness `cleanup`'s `viola-session-*` removal create and delete outside the working directory, each taking only a dir the test side itself made (by owner record, by its own `TempDir`, by the `viola-session-` name): a boundary widening, ratified by the founder (live, 2026-10-07T07:25Z, after it was shown to him as creating and deleting outside the working directory through the link; relayed by the overseer). No CI runner has a link, so CI's homes stay on the runner's disk. `cargo clean` removes the link, and the next start then makes a plain directory on the shared volume with no signal; one `ln -s` restores it.

subject: res-repository
text:
- `<repo parent>/viola-mutants-scratch/` (outside the repository, a sibling of it): the host mutation scratch. On a Windows host (`HOST_SCRATCH = cfg!(windows)`) `run --mutants` puts cargo-mutants' temp copies there (`TMP`/`TEMP` on the `cargo mutants` command) and its `--output`, so `mutants.out/` is `<scratch>/mutants.out/`. A guard refuses unless the resolved path's final component is exactly `viola-mutants-scratch` and the repository is neither it nor inside it (`scratch-refused`, never a fallback to `%TEMP%` or the repo). The scratch is measured, removed and recreated before every counted, scoped or package run (`scratch-wipe-failed` when the removal fails); the re-creation goes through `viola_state::fs::create_private_dir`, so on Windows the scratch is the topmost folder it creates outside the profile and takes the protected user + SYSTEM DACL, and every temp copy and test home laid inside it inherits owner-only, as one under `%TEMP%` does (a plain-created scratch on the runner's workspace drive inherits BUILTIN\Users write, which the instance check refuses `Writable`). The witness is `wipe_scratch_takes_an_instance_tree_the_check_accepts_where_a_plain_dir_does_not`, on CI's `test (windows-2025)` leg (as measured at ci#38375200217, chunk 2026-10-13-epoch-4-cleanup); whether the root package's Windows mutation baseline then reads green is not yet measured (the next `windows-mutants.yml` dispatch). Its path is never printed: documents carry only the byte count `scratch_bytes`. The dispatch-only `windows-mutants.yml` runs this same arm on the `windows-2025` runner, so there the scratch sits beside the runner's checkout (its parent directory); each job's document carries only `scratch_bytes` (0 on a fresh runner, as read in run 37174673472). Off Windows the harness arm is inert and `mutants.out/` stays at the repository root (gitignored).
 On the Linux dev host the same-named directory is the operator's `TMPDIR` for every mutation run — an environment fact, not harness code — and must be NOCOW (`chattr +C`): cargo-mutants 27.1.0 copies the tree (`target/` included, ~14 GB) into `std::env::temp_dir()`, `/tmp` there is a 32 GB `usrquota` tmpfs (a full viola-e2e run died at 460/709 on `Disk quota exceeded`), and on a COW btrfs dir its reflink copy drops the exec bit of the prebuilt `viola-fake-agent` (as measured at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-03-mutation-scoring-completion/evidence/m3.md`); a NOCOW dir makes the reflink fail over to the mode-keeping `fs::copy`. No document prints this path either.
